scope: Corollary 2.5 (Simultaneous model control) of the manuscript “Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity” (preprints/Orbifold-and-logarithmic-Iitaka-subadditivity-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b143366cc99615e1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose a smooth pair (X1, ∆1) has a fibration f1 : X1 → Y to a fixed smooth base, and every prime divisor contracted by f1 into codimension at least two has coefficient one in ∆1. Put C = B(f1, ∆1). Let a factorization through another smooth compact space be given, after an allowed source modification if necessary, by X1 g1 − → W1 h1 − → Y. Apply Theorem 2.4 to g1 and make any finite number of subsequent modifications of W1, always taking dominating smooth source models with reduced added exceptional boundaries. The resulting diagram X g − → W h − → Y , with source boundary ∆, can be chosen to have all the following properties: (i) Every prime contracted by g into codimension at least two is exceptional over the chosen smooth reference source for g1. (ii) Every prime contracted by f = h ◦ g into codimension at least two in Y has coefficient one in ∆. (iii) B(f, ∆) = C. In particular, for each prime D ⊂ Y and each prime E ⊂ X dominating D, (2.7) ordE(f∗ D) m∆(E) ≥ mC(D). (iv) The log Kodaira dimensions of the total source and of its very general fibers over Y are unchanged by these source modifications. The hypothesis on contracted divisors follows from Theorem 2.4, applied to the original map to its resolved base before fixing Y .
